Morgan / Rafael — detail on the unit-econ assumptions we used in the attached sheet. I kept this intentionally conservative for finance sign-off, with a parallel optimized scenario for engineering to consider. Key assumptions: 

1) Traffic and token math (monthly):
- Monthly interactions: 250k * 2.3 = 575k requests
- Avg in tokens: 450, avg gen: 120 -> 570 tokens per request total
- Monthly tokens: ~327M tokens (575k * 570)

2) Caching (prefix/KV) assumptions:
- Conservative: 0% cache hit (baseline)
- Optimized: 30% cache hit on input prefixes (Lumina has many repeated prompts), which reduces generation and KV lookup costs proportionally — effective tokens billed ~229M

3) Batching behavior (latency-targeted):
- Small-batch baseline: avg batch size 1.4 (low concurrency / strict p95 latency)
- Tuned dynamic batching: avg batch size 6.5 (server-side continuous batching, 60–90ms queue target)
- Batching increases throughput and reduces tokens/$ by better GPU packing; in our model batching yields ~18–28% cost reduction vs baseline, depending on model variant and sequence length distribution.

4) Model/variant and quantization:
- Baseline pricing assumes a mid-sized open model (FP16) with no aggressive quantization. We also show an option with 8-bit quant (savings 20–35% on serving compute).

5) Tokens / $ windows (examples from the spreadsheet):
- Baseline (no cache, small batch): ~0.55M tokens per $1 (range 0.48–0.62M depending on model)
- Optimized (30% cache, batching, quant): ~1.05M tokens per $1 (range 0.9–1.2M)

6) Sensitivity & guardrails:
- We include a stress test for 2x peak traffic and a fallback plan to a cheaper variant with graceful quality degradation.

Recommended next steps:
- Engineering: provide a 24–48 hour sample of production-like prompts so we can validate cache-hit assumptions (drive link in my attachment).
- Finance: decide which tokens/$ window you want to commit to for the MAP; we can model a blended commit that splits traffic across baseline and optimized configs during the POC to reduce variance.

I added detailed per-route timing and a simple cost dashboard tab in the spreadsheet. Happy to walk through the numbers on a 30-minute call.

— Soojin
Sr. Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Initial MAP ask — cost sanity for POC

Jordan — quick answers to help unblock procurement and security: 
- Cache hit semantics: the 30% figure in the optimized scenario primarily reduces input token billing (prefix/KV cache) — it also reduces the server work that leads to generation in many cases because repeated prompts short-circuit earlier. In practice we model both effects; see the "billing impact" column in the Lumina_MAP_v2 spreadsheet.
- Latency at avg batch 6.5: with Redwood continuous batching tuned to a 60ms queue target we observe p95s around 650–800ms on the model family we recommended (includes network + decode). Since you need p95 <750ms, we recommend a canary with warm KV cache and slightly tighter batch queue (40–60ms) during peak windows — that typically brings p95 into the <750ms band while preserving ~15–20% cost savings vs baseline.

We will add the SCQA and procurement sign-off rows to the MAP milestones and push an updated Lumina_MAP_v2 sheet by EOD Monday. Rafael — if Lumina is comfortable with the proposed timeline we can circulate a draft SOW and run the DocuSign loop next week.

— Ben
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
